question: For each rating category of the first movie rented by customers—where the first movie is identified based on the earliest payment date per customer—please provide the average total amount spent per customer and the average number of subsequent rentals (calculated as the total number of rentals minus one) for customers whose first rented movie falls into that rating category.
sql:
-- Step 4: Build the full query
-- Get customer-level metrics: total amount, total rentals
WITH earliest_payment AS (
    SELECT p.customer_id, p.payment_date, p.rental_id
    FROM payment p
    INNER JOIN (
        SELECT customer_id, MIN(payment_date) as min_date
        FROM payment
        GROUP BY customer_id
    ) ep ON p.customer_id = ep.customer_id AND p.payment_date = ep.min_date
),
first_rental AS (
    SELECT ep.customer_id, ep.payment_date, r.inventory_id, r.rental_id
    FROM earliest_payment ep
    JOIN rental r ON ep.rental_id = r.rental_id
),
first_rental_with_rating AS (
    SELECT fr.customer_id, fr.payment_date, fr.inventory_id, fr.rental_id, f.rating
    FROM first_rental fr
    JOIN inventory i ON fr.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
    JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
),
customer_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        SUM(amount) as total_amount,
        COUNT(*) as total_payments
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_rental_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        COUNT(*) as total_rentals
    FROM rental
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        frr.customer_id,
        frr.rating,
        ct.total_amount,
        crc.total_rentals,
        crc.total_rentals - 1 as subsequent_rentals
    FROM first_rental_with_rating frr
    JOIN customer_totals ct ON frr.customer_id = ct.customer_id
    JOIN customer_rental_counts crc ON frr.customer_id = crc.customer_id
)
SELECT 
    rating,
    AVG(total_amount) as avg_total_amount,
    AVG(subsequent_rentals) as avg_subsequent_rentals
FROM customer_metrics
GROUP BY rating
ORDER BY rating;
